name: DX - Financial Transformation (Phase 3, Asia Parks + Cruises)
brief: The customer needs a unified, governed data layer that standardizes source data, keeps reporting consistent across business units, performs well for BI at scale, and is ready for AI-assisted analysis.

plan.problem_statement: The customer needs a unified, governed data layer that standardizes source data, keeps reporting consistent across business units, performs well for BI at scale, and is ready for AI-assisted analysis.
decision_criteria_alignment: Unified architecture: Snowflake provides a single platform for ingestion, transformation, governance, and analytics, eliminating the need to manage multiple disparate tools
Native data sharing: Secure sharing between accounts and business units without data movement or duplication, enabling seamless cross-functional collaboration
Performance at scale: Dynamic Tables, Search Optimization, and intelligent caching deliver sub-second query response times even as data volumes grow
architecture_layers: Ingestion: Openflow — CDC connectors, incremental replication
Bronze: Iceberg Tables — raw landing tables, one schema per source
Silver: Dynamic Tables — conformed, deduplicated entities
Gold: Dynamic Tables — finance marts and aggregates
Semantic: Semantic Views — consistent business metrics
Sharing: Internal Marketplace — other business units
Governance: Row Access Policies — row-level security on gold
next_steps: Deploy Openflow CDC connectors for priority source systems; configure Snowpipe for cloud storage ingestion
Build Bronze layer (raw Iceberg Tables); create initial Dynamic Tables for Silver layer (deduplication, conformance)
Develop Gold layer aggregations with Dynamic Tables; deploy dbt Projects for version-controlled transformations
Define Semantic Views for key subject areas (revenue, operational metrics); deploy Cortex Agents for natural language query
Implement row access policies and masking policies for governance; enable Search Optimization on high-cardinality columns
Create secure shares for cross-unit collaboration; publish data products to Internal Marketplace
Set up custom budgets and resource monitors for cost governance; establish monitoring and alerting for data quality and pipeline health
Train team on CoCo skills for each capability area; establish prompt library and best practices documentation

sections.title: Data Ingestion: Real-Time CDC and Continuous Loading
sections.challenge: Multiple source systems (transactional databases, cloud storage, event streams) require automated, low-latency ingestion to support near-real-time reporting.
sections.explanation: Openflow provides change data capture (CDC) for databases, Snowpipe automates file ingestion from cloud storage, and Snowpipe Streaming handles high-throughput event data. Together, these capabilities eliminate manual data transfers and ensure fresh data availability.
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `openflow` skill to set up a CDC connector for your source database, the `snowpipe` skill to configure auto-ingest from cloud storage, and the `snowpipe-streaming` skill for real-time event ingestion.
sections.sql:
-- Openflow: Create destination database and grant permissions
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS finance_raw;

GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE finance_raw TO ROLE OPENFLOW_FINANCE_CDC_EXECUTE_AS_RL;
GRANT CREATE SCHEMA ON DATABASE finance_raw TO ROLE OPENFLOW_FINANCE_CDC_EXECUTE_AS_RL;

-- Create ingest warehouse for the connector
CREATE WAREHOUSE openflow_ingest_wh
  WITH
    WAREHOUSE_SIZE = 'XSMALL'
    AUTO_SUSPEND = 300
    AUTO_RESUME = TRUE;

GRANT USAGE, OPERATE ON WAREHOUSE openflow_ingest_wh TO ROLE OPENFLOW_FINANCE_CDC_EXECUTE_AS_RL;

-- Snowpipe: Create external stage over cloud storage
CREATE STAGE finance_raw.public.orders_stage
  URL = 's3://finance-data-bucket/orders/'
  STORAGE_INTEGRATION = finance_s3_int;

-- Create auto-ingest pipe
CREATE PIPE finance_raw.public.orders_pipe
  AUTO_INGEST = TRUE
  AS
  COPY INTO finance_raw.public.raw_orders
    FROM @finance_raw.public.orders_stage
    FILE_FORMAT = (TYPE = 'JSON')
    MATCH_BY_COLUMN_NAME = CASE_INSENSITIVE;

-- Snowpipe Streaming: Custom pipe for high-performance ingestion
CREATE OR REPLACE PIPE finance_raw.public.events_streaming_pipe AS
    COPY INTO finance_raw.public.raw_events (event_id, event_type, event_data, event_timestamp)
    FROM (SELECT $1:event_id, $1:event_type, $1:event_data, $1:event_timestamp);
notes: Openflow requires a runtime with execute-as role; follow the setup wizard for connector-specific configuration
Snowpipe auto-ingest requires cloud event notifications (SQS for S3, Event Grid for Azure)
Snowpipe Streaming high-performance architecture requires Iceberg Tables
Monitor pipe status: SELECT SYSTEM$PIPE_STATUS('finance_raw.public.orders_pipe');

sections.title: Data Transformation: Declarative Pipelines and Orchestration
sections.challenge: Traditional ETL scripts require manual dependency management, frequent rewrites, and long refresh cycles, slowing time-to-insight.
sections.explanation: Dynamic Tables provide declarative, SQL-based transformations with automatic dependency resolution and incremental refresh. Tasks orchestrate non-SQL workloads (Snowpark, stored procedures). dbt Projects enable version-controlled, Git-based transformation workflows with CI/CD integration.
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `dynamic-tables` skill to create incremental transformation pipelines, the `snowflake-tasks` skill for orchestration, and the `dbt-projects-on-snowflake` skill to deploy Git-managed dbt models.
sections.sql:
-- Dynamic Tables: Bronze to Silver (latest row per key, SCD Type 1)
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE finance_silver.customers_current
    TARGET_LAG = '10 minutes'
    WAREHOUSE = transform_wh
    REFRESH_MODE = INCREMENTAL
AS
    SELECT * EXCLUDE (raw_metadata_col)
    FROM finance_raw.customers_cdc
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY updated_at DESC
    ) = 1;

-- Dynamic Tables: Silver to Gold (aggregations with downstream lag)
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE finance_silver.orders_enriched
    TARGET_LAG = DOWNSTREAM
    WAREHOUSE = transform_wh
    REFRESH_MODE = INCREMENTAL
AS
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        o.order_date,
        o.quantity,
        o.unit_price,
        o.quantity * o.unit_price AS line_total,
        c.region,
        c.segment
    FROM finance_raw.orders o
    JOIN finance_silver.customers_current c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE finance_gold.orders_daily
    TARGET_LAG = '30 minutes'
    WAREHOUSE = transform_wh
    REFRESH_MODE = INCREMENTAL
AS
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('day', order_date) AS order_day,
        region,
        segment,
        COUNT(*) AS order_count,
        SUM(line_total) AS daily_revenue
    FROM finance_silver.orders_enriched
    GROUP BY ALL;

-- dbt Projects: Deploy Git-managed transformations
CREATE DBT PROJECT finance_db.dbt_schema.finance_models
  FROM '@finance_db.integrations.dbt_git_stage/branches/main'
  DEFAULT_TARGET = 'prod'
  EXTERNAL_ACCESS_INTEGRATIONS = 'dbt_external_access'
  COMMENT = 'Finance data models.';

-- Schedule dbt project with a task
CREATE OR ALTER TASK finance_db.dbt_schema.run_finance_models
  WAREHOUSE = transform_wh
  SCHEDULE = '6 hours'
AS
  EXECUTE DBT PROJECT finance_db.dbt_schema.finance_models args='run --target prod';
notes: TARGET_LAG = DOWNSTREAM for intermediate layers allows Snowflake to optimize refresh automatically
REFRESH_MODE = INCREMENTAL requires base tables to support change tracking (native tables, Iceberg, Streams)
dbt Projects require a Git stage and external access integration for repository access
CoCo can generate both Dynamic Tables and dbt models from natural language descriptions

sections.title: Analytics & Reporting: Semantic Layer and Conversational AI
sections.challenge: Inconsistent metric definitions across teams, slow ad-hoc queries, and limited self-service capabilities hinder business agility.
sections.explanation: Semantic Views define a single source of truth for metrics, dimensions, and relationships in YAML. Cortex Agents enable business users to query data using natural language, translating questions into optimized SQL via the Cortex Analyst tool. This combination accelerates insight generation and reduces reliance on data teams.
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `agent-studio` skill to create a Semantic View with tables, relationships, metrics, and dimensions, then deploy a Cortex Agent with a Cortex Analyst tool to enable natural language query.
sections.sql:
-- Semantic View: Define business metrics and relationships
CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW finance_gold.revenue_analysis

  TABLES (
    orders AS finance_gold.orders_daily
      PRIMARY KEY (order_day, region, segment)
      COMMENT = 'Daily aggregated order data',
    customers AS finance_silver.customers_current
      PRIMARY KEY (customer_id)
      COMMENT = 'Current customer snapshot'
  )

  RELATIONSHIPS (
    orders_to_customers AS
      orders (segment) REFERENCES customers
  )

  FACTS (
    orders.order_count,
    orders.daily_revenue
  )

  DIMENSIONS (
    orders.order_day
      COMMENT = 'Date of the orders',
    orders.region
      COMMENT = 'Geographic region',
    orders.segment
      COMMENT = 'Customer segment'
  )

  METRICS (
    orders.total_revenue AS SUM(orders.daily_revenue)
      COMMENT = 'Total revenue across all orders',
    orders.average_order_value AS AVG(orders.daily_revenue / orders.order_count)
      COMMENT = 'Average revenue per order'
  )

  COMMENT = 'Semantic view for revenue analysis';

-- Cortex Agent: Deploy conversational analytics agent
CREATE OR REPLACE SECURE AGENT finance_analytics_agent
  COMMENT = 'Natural language query agent for finance reporting.'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: claude-sonnet-4-6
  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: "cortex_analyst_text_to_sql"
        name: "RevenueAnalyst"
  tool_resources:
    RevenueAnalyst:
      semantic_view: "finance_gold.revenue_analysis"
  $$;

-- Grant access and preserve grants on replace
GRANT USAGE ON AGENT finance_analytics_agent TO ROLE finance_analyst_role;

CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT finance_analytics_agent COPY GRANTS
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: claude-sonnet-4-6
  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: "cortex_analyst_text_to_sql"
        name: "RevenueAnalyst"
  tool_resources:
    RevenueAnalyst:
      semantic_view: "finance_gold.revenue_analysis"
  $$;
notes: Semantic Views support synonyms, custom instructions, and verified query repositories for improved agent accuracy
Cortex Agents can use multiple tools; extend with custom MCP servers for external data sources or APIs
Grant USAGE on the agent to roles; use COPY GRANTS when replacing to preserve existing permissions

sections.title: Lakehouse Architecture: Open Formats and Interoperability
sections.challenge: Data silos across platforms prevent unified analytics and limit flexibility for data science workflows.
sections.explanation: Iceberg Tables enable an open lakehouse architecture with cross-platform compatibility. Snowflake Notebooks provide interactive Python/SQL environments for exploratory analysis and ML workflows. This combination supports diverse analytical workloads on a single copy of data.
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `iceberg` skill to create Iceberg Tables for open lakehouse storage and the `snowflake-notebooks` skill to build interactive Python/SQL workflows.
sections.sql:
-- Iceberg Table: Snowflake-managed with external volume
CREATE ICEBERG TABLE finance_raw.events_iceberg (
  event_id STRING,
  event_type STRING,
  event_data VARIANT,
  event_timestamp TIMESTAMP
)
  CATALOG = 'SNOWFLAKE'
  EXTERNAL_VOLUME = 'SNOWFLAKE_MANAGED';

-- Notebook: Create from a stage
CREATE NOTEBOOK finance_analysis.notebooks.revenue_exploration
 FROM '@finance_db.public.notebook_stage'
 MAIN_FILE = 'revenue_analysis.ipynb'
 QUERY_WAREHOUSE = analytics_wh;
notes: Snowpipe Streaming high-performance architecture works with Iceberg Tables for low-latency ingestion
Notebooks support Snowpark Python for distributed compute and external package installation
Iceberg Tables can be queried from external engines (Spark, Trino) via catalog integrations

sections.title: Cross-Unit Collaboration: Secure Sharing and Internal Marketplace
sections.challenge: Data duplication and manual sharing processes create latency, inconsistency, and governance risks across business units.
sections.explanation: Secure Data Sharing enables live, governed access to data without copying or moving it. Organizational Listings (Internal Marketplace) provide a self-service catalog for discovering and requesting access to shared data products within the same organization.
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `data-sharing` skill to create secure shares for cross-account collaboration and the Internal Marketplace to publish data products for self-service discovery.
notes: Organizational Listings enable self-service discovery of shared data products
Shares can include tables, secure views, secure functions, and Cortex Agents
Row access policies and masking policies apply to shared objects, ensuring governed access
Data Clean Rooms provide privacy-preserving collaboration for sensitive data (GA)

sections.title: Query Performance: Search Optimization for High-Cardinality Dimensions
sections.challenge: Dashboards and ad-hoc queries on large tables with high-cardinality columns experience timeouts and slow response times.
sections.explanation: The Search Optimization Service accelerates point lookups, selective filters, and joins on high-cardinality columns by maintaining a search access path. This is especially effective for dimensions with millions of unique values (customer IDs, product SKUs, transaction IDs).
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `search_optimization` CoCo skill (if available) or manually enable search optimization on high-cardinality columns using ALTER TABLE.
notes: Search Optimization Service requires Enterprise Edition or higher
Best for columns with cardinality > 100,000 used in equality filters or joins
Adds incremental storage and maintenance cost; monitor cost via ACCOUNT_USAGE.SEARCH_OPTIMIZATION_HISTORY
Combine with clustering keys for optimal performance on frequently filtered columns

sections.title: Data Governance: Row Access Policies and Dynamic Masking
sections.challenge: Using views for row-level security prevents partition pruning and metadata optimization, causing performance degradation as data scales.
sections.explanation: Row access policies attach directly to tables and views, applying filtering logic at query time while preserving partition pruning and metadata operations. Dynamic data masking protects sensitive columns based on role. Memoizable functions optimize policy lookups by caching authorization checks.
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `data-governance` skill to create row access policies with mapping tables and attach them to tables/views. Use memoizable functions for policy logic that performs authorization lookups.
sections.sql:
-- Create a mapping table for region-based access
CREATE TABLE finance_security.region_access (
  user_role STRING,
  allowed_region STRING
);

-- Insert access rules
INSERT INTO finance_security.region_access VALUES
  ('FINANCE_ANALYST_APAC', 'Asia Pacific'),
  ('FINANCE_ANALYST_EMEA', 'Europe');

-- Memoizable function for efficient policy lookups
CREATE FUNCTION finance_security.is_region_authorized(region VARCHAR)
RETURNS BOOLEAN
MEMOIZABLE
AS
$$
  SELECT ARRAY_CONTAINS(
    region::VARIANT,
    (SELECT ARRAY_AGG(allowed_region) FROM finance_security.region_access WHERE user_role = CURRENT_ROLE())
  )
$$;

-- Row access policy using the memoizable function
CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY finance_security.region_policy
AS (region_col VARCHAR) RETURNS BOOLEAN ->
  'ACCOUNTADMIN' = CURRENT_ROLE()
  OR finance_security.is_region_authorized(region_col);

-- Attach policy to table
ALTER TABLE finance_gold.orders_daily ADD ROW ACCESS POLICY finance_security.region_policy ON (region);

-- Masking policy for sensitive columns
CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY finance_security.customer_email_mask AS (val STRING) RETURNS STRING ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('FINANCE_ADMIN', 'COMPLIANCE_ANALYST') THEN val
    ELSE '*********'
  END;

-- Attach masking policy to column
ALTER TABLE finance_silver.customers_current MODIFY COLUMN email
  SET MASKING POLICY finance_security.customer_email_mask;
notes: Row access policies and masking require Enterprise Edition or higher
Memoizable functions cache results within a query, reducing repeated policy evaluations
Policies apply to all queries, including shared data; consumers inherit producer governance rules
Use object tags to classify data and automate policy attachment (e.g., PII tag -> masking policy)

sections.title: Cost Management: Budgets and Resource Monitors
sections.challenge: Unpredictable resource consumption as workloads scale, with limited visibility into cost drivers and no proactive controls.
sections.explanation: Custom Budgets provide configurable thresholds and notifications for credit usage across accounts, warehouses, or custom resource groups. Resource Monitors enforce hard limits by suspending warehouses when quotas are reached. Together, these tools enable proactive cost governance.
sections.coco_prompt: Use the `cost-intelligence` skill to create custom budgets with alerts and resource monitors with automatic suspension policies.
notes: Custom Budgets support account, warehouse, and user-level tracking
Resource Monitors can suspend, suspend immediately, or notify at configurable thresholds
Combine with per-user quotas for granular cost attribution
Monitor credit usage: SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY;
